claims.text: With the default restartPolicy (Always), when a container exits the kubelet starts it again inside the same Pod (same name, uid and IP address) and the container's restart count (RESTARTS) increases.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Lifecycle (Container restart policy; default Always); outputs liveness.txt (same uid/IP)

claims.text: A restart of a container in its Pod creates no new Pod, so the ReplicaSet does not act.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Lifecycle (restarts are handled by the kubelet within the Pod); ReplicaSet (replaces Pods, not containers)

claims.text: The first restart after a crash is immediate; for a container that keeps stopping, later restarts get an exponential back-off delay, and while the kubelet waits the Pod shows CrashLoopBackOff.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Lifecycle (exponential back-off; CrashLoopBackOff); outputs liveness.txt

claims.text: A probe is a diagnostic the kubelet performs periodically on a container; an httpGet probe sends an HTTP GET to a path and port of the container.
An httpGet probe succeeds if the response status code is >= 200 and < 400; any other status, or no answer within the timeout, is a failure.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Lifecycle (Check mechanisms: httpGet 'greater than or equal to 200 and less than 400'); probes timeoutSeconds

claims.text: After failureThreshold consecutive liveness failures (default 3), the kubelet kills the container and it is restarted per restartPolicy.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes (failureThreshold default 3; liveness restart)

claims.text: Restarting api containers cannot bring back PostgreSQL; a liveness probe on a database check would restart every api container during an outage.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io probes guidance (liveness should not depend on external dependencies); health-endpoints lesson

claims.text: web-liveness-pod.yaml@stage-2: Pod web-liveness, caddy:2.10.0, livenessProbe httpGet /healthz port 80; Caddy's default site answers 404 for /healthz.

liveness.sh@stage-2 lines 12-35: applies the Pod, stores uid and IP, waits for restartCount >= 1, compares uid/IP, waits for waiting.reason CrashLoopBackOff; then prints probe events, deletes the Pod and greps describe of Deployment api.
Every object has a metadata.uid that is unique; the same uid means the same Pod object.

liveness.txt@stage-2: RESTARTS 1, same uid yes, same IP yes, CrashLoopBackOff; events Killing ('failed liveness probe, will be restarted') and Unhealthy ('statuscode: 404'); api Liveness http-get :8080/health/live ... #failure=3.

deploy/k8s/api.yaml@stage-2: the api container's livenessProbe is httpGet path /health/live port 8080; kubectl describe shows probe defaults filled in (delay=0s timeout=1s period=10s #success=1 #failure=3).
claims.source_hint: git -C examples/don-hang show stage-2:deploy/k8s/api.yaml lines 45-48; outputs liveness.txt

claims.text: kubectl get -w on web-liveness for ~5 min: same name, RESTARTS rising about every 30 s at first; after a few restarts CrashLoopBackOff appears between restarts and the gaps grow (observed on kind v1.34.11).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io Pod Lifecycle (back-off); run of web-liveness-pod.yaml on kind

claims.text: Events are short records Kubernetes keeps of what happened to an object; a failed liveness probe produces Unhealthy and Killing events for the Pod.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: kubectl events / Pod Lifecycle; outputs liveness.txt

claims.text: kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/<name> waits until the Pod's Ready condition is True (its container started and, with no readiness probe, counts as ready).
claims.source_hint: kubectl wait reference; kubernetes.io Pod Lifecycle (Pod conditions: Ready)

claims.text: kubectl get -w (--watch) keeps running and prints a line whenever the listed object changes.
